chapter_theme: Petty knowledge that thinks itself wise. It is the poverty that counts most, it does worse harm than any enemy, and it can't be taught, because the person who has it is already sure that he knows.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar: its defect (841), its inability to do good to oneself and its doing of harm (842-843), self-admiration (844-846), and refusal of good counsel (847-850).

841.reading: Lack of understanding is the poverty of poverties; other lack the world does not count as lack.
841.nuance: வையாது உலகு attributes the valuation to the world. Parimelazhagar's reason is that the wise keep this world's and the next world's fruit even in poverty, whereas the petty-minded don't even with wealth.

842.reading: When a person without understanding gives with a glad heart, the cause is nothing other than the receiver's merit.
842.nuance: A strange and rather cold claim: a good act by such a person earns him nothing. Parimelazhagar raises and rebuts the objection that fools also do good. Kalaignar has simply good luck (பெற்றபேறு), which removes தவம் from the picture.

843.reading: The suffering those without understanding do to themselves is hard even for their enemies to do.
843.nuance: Parimelazhagar gives a clever reason: an enemy has to watch for a moment and knows only so much, whereas self-injury never pauses and reaches poverty, blame and sin all at once.

844.reading: What is called வெண்மை? It is the pride that says 'we have brightness.'
844.nuance: வெண்மை, whiteness, is rawness or unripeness. ஒண்மை is brightness. The two words sound alike and describe opposite things, and the fool can't tell whether he is lit or blank. Parimelazhagar calls it a delusion because such people persist knowing the world mocks them.

845.reading: Taking on what one hasn't learned brings doubt even on what one has mastered without flaw.
845.nuance: The verse is about how credibility works. The pretence costs real knowledge too. This is not a moral claim but a practical one about reputation, and it grants that the pretender may have actual skill.

846.reading: Is covering one's nakedness not itself petty, when one's faults aren't covered?

positions.position: To cover a fault means to get rid of it. Covering the lesser thing while leaving the greater and thinking oneself decent is the folly.
To cover a fault means keeping it from others' notice, as clothing hides the body from view.
positions.quote: தம்பாலுள்ள குற்றத்தைப் பிறரறியாமல் தாம் மறையாத காலத் து

847.reading: One without understanding who lets slip the precious மறை does great harm to himself by himself.

positions.position: மறை is rare teaching which the fool doesn't take in. He rejects the other reading explicitly, since leaking a secret would be carelessness and not this fault.
positions.quote: அது பேணாமை என்னும் பேதைமையாவதன்றிப் புல்லறிவாண்மையன்மை அறிக.

positions.position: மறை is a closely held secret, and letting it slip means telling others.

848.reading: Not doing it when told, not seeing it himself, that life is a disease until it departs.
848.nuance: The verse doesn't say for whom. Parimelazhagar says for the earth that bears him, Manakkudavar for the people of the world, and Kalaignar for himself. These are three very different diseases. The verse's two failures also cover both routes to knowledge, one's own and another's.

849.reading: One who shows things to a person who doesn't see becomes himself unseeing, and the unseeing one goes on having seen what he saw.
849.nuance: The compact wordplay on காண் is the content: the teacher fails and the pupil remains satisfied. Parimelazhagar says the teacher is blamed by the pupil and ends up the ignorant one, and concludes that good sense can't be instilled here by any means.

850.reading: One who says 'it isn't' to what the world says is will be set down on this earth as a demon.
850.nuance: The verse names neither what's denied nor who 'the world' is, and everything turns on those blanks.

positions.position: What is denied is God, rebirth, and the fruit of deeds, as affirmed by the eminent.
positions.quote: கடவுளும், மறுபிறப்பும், இருவினைப் பயனும் முதலாக அவர் உள என்பன பலவேனும்

positions.position: What is denied is what the many wise affirm, with no specific doctrine named.
positions.quote: உலகத்தில் அறிவுடையார் பலர் உண்டென்பதாகிய ஒரு பொருளை இல்லையென்று

positions.position: What is denied is what's been shown clearly by evidence, and the denial is deliberate.
positions.quote: ஆதாரங்களைக் காட்டி இதுதான் உண்மை என்று தெளிவாகக் கூறப்படுகிற ஒன்றை

links.note: Two reports of what the world does. 752 says everyone despises those with nothing. 841 says the world doesn't count lack of wealth as lack. Both can't be plain observation, so at least one of them is the Kural speaking for how the world ought to judge.

Same doubled form (இன்மையுள் இன்மை, இன்மையின் இன்மை). 1041 says the only thing as painful as poverty is poverty. 841 gives the title to lack of understanding. The chapter on poverty and this one rank the worst lack differently.

850 makes denying the world's consensus demonic. 423 says wisdom is finding the truth in anything, whoever says it. Parimelazhagar's doctrinal list sharpens this, and Kalaignar's 'evidence' moves 850 closer to 423.

Both are about the garment and the shame of exposure. In 788 a friend's help comes as fast as the hand to a slipping cloth. In 846 the cloth over the body is exposed as a fraud if faults stay bare. One makes the reflex an ideal and the other mocks it as a substitute.
